explanation: India's density rose from 117 persons per sq km in 1951 to 382 in 2011.

notes.text: - **Least populous units:** **Lakshadweep (64,429)**, Daman and Diu, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, Sikkim, Chandigarh; Lakshadweep was also the least populous UT in **2001**.

q: According to 2001 Census, the Indian state with highest density of population per sq. km
explanation: In Census 2001 West Bengal (904) had the highest density among States, ahead of Bihar (880) and Kerala (819); Bihar overtook it in 2011.

exam: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon (Specialist) in AP Vaidya Vidh
q: After reorganization, what is the position of Andhra Pradesh State amongst the States of the Country in terms of population?
explanation: After the 2014 bifurcation, residual Andhra Pradesh (4.95 crore, about 4.1%) is the 10th most populous State; undivided AP had been 5th.

notes.text: - Big but thinly peopled: Rajasthan (largest, only 5.5% of people), J&K, Arunachal, Uttarakhand.

q: Which of the following states has the least population?
explanation:
Jammu and Kashmir was a State in 2003 — now a Union Territory (since 31 October 2019, J&K Reorganisation Act 2019) (general knowledge, not checked)
Jammu and Kashmir (about 1.0 crore in 2001, 1.25 crore in 2011) has fewer people than Haryana, Gujarat and Rajasthan (it has been a UT since 2019).

notes.text: > Dispute: Kutch is the usual answer for the largest district; Leh's official area including territory under foreign occupation is larger, but Census 2011 gave Leh 45,110 sq km.

q: As per the 2001 Census, Uttar Pradesh is the most populous state. Which states occupy second and third place?
explanation: Census 2001 ranking: Uttar Pradesh 1st, Maharashtra 2nd, Bihar 3rd, West Bengal 4th; the order was the same in 2011.

notes.text: - **Descending area:** Chhattisgarh (1.35 lakh) > Jharkhand (79,716) > Himachal Pradesh (55,673) > Uttarakhand (53,483) sq km; Uttarakhand is far smaller than UP, MP and Rajasthan.

q: According to the 2001 Census, the Union Territo with lowest population in India is
explanation: Lakshadweep was the least populous UT in 2001 (about 61,000) and in 2011 (64,429); Chandigarh, Puducherry and Delhi are far larger.

q: Governmental efforts to improve the quality of life is hindered by growing
explanation: Growing population pressure on limited resources hinders government efforts to raise the quality of life. Urbanisation and technology are not the main brake.

notes.text: - Growing **population pressure** hinders government efforts to improve the quality of life (APPSC Group II 2011).
